questions.question: What does linearity of expectation state for finite expectations?
Does linearity of expectation require independence?
What condition is required for applying linearity of expectation?
options: The variables have the same distribution

questions.question: For random variables $X,Y$ with finite variances, which additional assumption guarantees $\operatorname{Var}(X+Y)=\operatorname{Var}(X)+\operatorname{Var}(Y)$?
options: nothing more than finite variances of $X$ and $Y$

questions.question: If a count is written as a sum of indicators $X=I_1+\cdots+I_n$, why can $E[X]$ be computed by adding the individual indicator expectations?
If $E[X]=2$ and $E[Y]=5$, what is $E[X+Y]$?
If $E[X]=3$, what is $E[4X]$?
If $E[X]=1$ and $E[Y]=2$, what is $E[3X+4Y]$?
What is the expected number of heads in ten fair tosses using indicators?
options: The product of ten head-indicator expectations
The sum of ten head-indicator expectations
The expectation of only the first toss

questions.question: For a random variable $X$ with finite expectation $E[X]=\mu$ and real constants $a,b$, what is $E[aX+b]$?
Why is independence not needed for linearity of expectation?
options: Linearity concerns averages of sums, not products of variables
All random variables are independent by definition

questions.question: What is the common mistake when applying linearity?
options: Adding the expected costs of the individual components to get a total

questions.question: Why are indicator variables useful with linearity?
options: They remove the need for probabilities
Complex totals can be decomposed into simple zero-one contributions
They turn all expectations into variances, which are easier to add up

questions.question: If $E[X]=4$ and $E[Y]=-1$, what is $E[2X-3Y]$?
A total number of occupied boxes is written as $I_1+\cdots+I_n$. How can its expectation be computed?
options: As zero unless all boxes are occupied

questions.question: If $X$ and $Y$ are dependent but have finite expectations $1$ and $6$, what is $E[X+Y]$?
Linearity of expectation holds for finite sums but does not extend automatically to infinite ones. Where does the finite-sum version stop?
options: It automatically applies to every infinite sum
It requires all variables to be independent
It applies to finite sums with finite expectations
It only applies when all coefficients are positive

questions.question: Why does linearity make expectation calculations modular?
options: One must compute the full joint distribution first in every case
One can compute expected parts separately and then add them

questions.question: If $E[X]=2$, $E[Y]=3$, and $E[Z]=4$, what is $E[X+Y+Z]$?
A solution refuses to use linearity because two indicators are dependent. What is the issue?
options: Dependent indicators must have equal means before linearity can be used
Dependence is not a barrier to linearity of expectation
